pass_summary: Re-review after fixes. All three previous must_fix findings are resolved: defaultExecutor now uses execFileSync with an argv array (no shell), create()/remove() refuse and log when config.directory is null (no '' / '.' fallbacks), and create() logs success and failure. The two un-awaited .resolves assertions are awaited, and the new tests cover the null-directory, metacharacter-name, executor-failure and abandon-failure paths. register-plan/baseRef are now honestly in Out of Scope, and the Task 4 manual items stay unticked with partial evidence. target() and configure() are unchanged by the diff (no regression). One new should_fix: with stdio 'ignore' the CLI's own stderr is still thrown away, so every create failure is logged as a possible PATH problem even when the real cause is something else (dirty checkout, slot limit, git error). The other new findings are minor: Windows .cmd resolution, an option-shaped slug, the blocking synchronous spawn, and stale bundles.

issues.title: stdio: 'ignore' still discards the CLI's stderr, and the PATH hint is shown for every failure
issues.description: makeDefaultExecutor runs `execFileSync(cmd, args, { stdio: "ignore" })`. When `sentinal` is found but `worktree create` exits non-zero (dirty main checkout, BASE_CHECKED_OUT, slot pool exhausted, invalid ref from a free-text name such as '..'), the thrown error's message is only 'Command failed: sentinal worktree create …'. stderr was not captured, so the real reason is lost. create() then logs 'workspace create failed (is `sentinal` in PATH? …)' for every failure, which points the user at the wrong cause. A true PATH miss shows up as `err.code === "ENOENT"` (spawnSync ENOENT); every other failure has a numeric `status`.
issues.suggested_fix: In makeDefaultExecutor use `stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "pipe"]` (or `"pipe"`) and include `String(err.stderr ?? "").trim()` (truncated, e.g. last 500 chars) in the rethrown/logged message. In create() add the PATH hint only when `(e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"`; otherwise log `workspace create failed for spec/<slug>: <stderr>`. Add a test where the executor throws an error with `status: 1, stderr: "dirty checkout"` and assert the log contains 'dirty checkout' and not 'PATH'.

issues.title: Windows: execFileSync without a shell does not resolve `sentinal.cmd` npm shims
issues.description: The old execSync went through cmd.exe, which resolves `sentinal` to `sentinal.cmd`/PATHEXT. execFileSync('sentinal', …) with no shell only finds a real `sentinal.exe`, so on Windows an npm/bun-installed shim now fails with ENOENT. That is a Windows-only regression, made less visible because the PATH hint fits it exactly. The repo already treats Windows as a lesser-supported platform (worker-access falls back to a plain command there), so this is low impact.
issues.suggested_fix: On `process.platform === "win32"`, run `cmd.exe /d /s /c sentinal …` with each argument quoted, or resolve the shim explicitly (try `sentinal.cmd`). Alternatively, document Windows as unsupported for the workspace adaptor in the file header.

issues.title: Option-shaped slug from the free-text name reaches commander as a flag
issues.description: There is no shell any more, so this is no longer command injection. But a dialog name with no '/' that starts with '-' (for example '--base=main' or '--json') becomes the slug argv element, and commander parses it as an option rather than as <slug>. Today that only produces a CLI error, which is logged. No slug validation exists anywhere downstream either: grep finds none in src/worktree.
issues.suggested_fix: Validate the slug before exec (e.g. `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/`, log and return otherwise), or insert a `--` end-of-options marker if the worktree create command supports it.

issues.title: create() spawns synchronously with no timeout, so it blocks the plugin process during worktree setup
issues.description: This predates the fix (execSync had the same problem). `sentinal worktree create` also runs the runtime contract's `setup` (this repo's is `bun install --frozen-lockfile`), so execFileSync can block OpenCode's plugin event loop for tens of seconds, and indefinitely if a step hangs.
issues.suggested_fix: Pass a `timeout` (e.g. 120_000) to execFileSync, or switch to async `execFile`/`Bun.spawn` and await it, since create() is already async.

issues.title: Rebuild the shipped bundles before release
issues.description: Only src/opencode/* and the plan changed. The bundled plugin copies (targets/opencode/dist/sentinal.mjs and the plugin embedded in src/cli/embedded-assets.ts, which contains createSpecWorktreeAdaptor) still have the pre-fix executor until `bun run build:opencode` and `embed-assets` run. CI's check-embed-assets should catch this, but users should not get the shell-string version from a stale artifact.
issues.suggested_fix: Run `bun run build:all` (and embed-assets) before committing, and include the regenerated artifacts if they are tracked.
